newsitem.title: USA: New York City says 140 retirees 'double-dipped'.
newsitem.headline: New York City says 140 retirees 'double-dipped'.

text.p: New York City's Comptroller said Thursday that 140 city retirees illegally collected both a pension and a paycheck from New York City or New York State, a practice called "double-dipping."

One city sanitation worker got $145,458 in overpayments from 1990 to 1996. In that period, the individual received a city disability pension while also working for the State Division of Youth. Present and future pension payments to this person have been suspended.

"There are reasonable rules that permit exceptions, and there are no excuses for not following them. But when we examined how many city pensioners were working for the state or back with the city, we found substantial abuse," said Alan Hevesi, city comptroller, in prepared remarks.

The 69 double-dippers, who worked for the state in 1993, 1994 and 1995, collected $1.49 million in illegal city pension payments, said Hevesi, who conducted the first audit that cross-checked city pensioners against a list of state workers. Most of the state retirees had worked for the police department, as 38 fell into that category.

The 71 double-dippers who went back to work for the city in 1995 received another $410,000 in illegal pension payments during that year. Teachers edged out former police workers in this grouping, as there were 25 retired teachers and 21 retirees from the police force.

Hevesi said that officials of all five city pension funds agreed to calculate the overpayments and recover them, adding his previous audits of double-dippers recovered substantial amounts. The comptroller said the funds also agreed to "reinforce" to governmental agencies the importance of having effective procedures to prevent such abuses and to remind retirees of the law.
